title: Gideon and the Regiment
premise: In the final winter of the Republic of Vessany, courier Zephyrine Iversen carries sealed dispatches through a capital sliding into martial law, guided by three years of learned silences. When an abandoned child arrives at his door clutching a cipher that matches the one hidden in his own dispatch case, Zephyrine realizes the regiment he has faithfully served is the author of the atrocity the documents expose. Torn between loyalty to Colonel Aurel Vance—the man who trained him and whom he secretly loves—and the truth that could save thousands, Zephyrine smuggles the evidence past three checkpoints as the city falls. He delivers it at terrible cost: Vance chooses duty over love and dies holding the gate open, while Zephyrine escapes with the child, carrying both the truth and the inheritance of everything the republic failed to be.
about_author: Tamsin Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing diplomatic correspondence from collapsed states before turning to fiction. She writes from a coastal town where she keeps, by her own account, too many unfinished maps.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He crosses a frozen checkpoint with dispatches sewn into his coat, narrating the rules of silence that keep couriers alive. At his lodging he finds a child asleep on his doorstep with a note: forget the face. The beat is wary tenderness—his carefully ordered world cracking open on page one.

chapters.title: Instructions to Forget
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He cannot find the boy's origin; the note's paper bears a regimental watermark. Colonel Aurel Vance summons him, assigns the final mission—three checkpoints to the neutral embassy—and their charged, restrained reunion reveals the love neither names. Beat: longing sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Cipher Says
chapters.summary: Dual POV begins alternating with the child, Milo, who speaks in fragments of a village that no longer exists. Zephyrine decodes the boy's cipher against his own dispatches and finds orders for the Kesselra evacuation massacre—signed by Vance's superior, countersigned in Vance's hand. Beat: vertigo of betrayed trust.

chapters.title: Loyalty Is a Kind of Blindness
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. He suspects Zephyrine knows, and interrogates him gently over wine, each man lying beautifully. Flashbacks to their first meeting reveal how Vance shaped Zephyrine's silences. Beat: intimacy weaponized, both men aware they are being tested and refusing to fail openly.

chapters.title: First Checkpoint: The Bridge of Sighs
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. He moves at night with Milo disguised as his nephew, hiding the evidence inside a dead man's coffin requisitioned through regimental channels. A search nearly finds them; a sympathetic sergeant looks away. Beat: fear transmuted into cunning, the first proof he can outthink the machine.

chapters.title: The Inheritance of Ash
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Through the child's eyes we see the burned village and the soldier who carried him out—a man wearing Vance's insignia. Zephyrine confronts the possibility that Vance saved Milo even while signing the order. Beat: moral complexity deepening; hatred refuses to settle into a simple shape.

chapters.title: Second Checkpoint: The Custom House
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Martial law tightens; the custom house demands papers for two. He trades his mother's ring—the last inheritance he owns—to a forger, and learns Vance has flagged his route for 'protection.' Is it surveillance or shelter? Beat: paranoia braided with hope.

chapters.title: Confession at the Wall
chapters.summary: Vance's POV. Cornering Zephyrine before the final checkpoint, Vance admits he signed under duress but has been quietly sabotaging the operation for months—he left the child at the door. He offers Zephyrine escape without the documents. Zephyrine refuses. Beat: the love declared precisely as duty divides them.

chapters.title: Third Checkpoint: The Gate of the Fallen
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The city rises; the third checkpoint becomes a battlefield. Vance seizes command of the gate, orders his own soldiers to stand down, and holds the passage open under fire so Zephyrine and Milo can reach the embassy. Beat: climax—sacrifice as the only honest answer to a corrupt oath.

chapters.title: Everything That Survives Us
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV, epilogue in spring. The documents reach foreign presses; the republic falls but its crimes are named. Zephyrine raises Milo in exile, teaching him new silences and when not to keep them. On the boy's desk lies Vance's compass, inherited. Beat: grief resolved into guardianship—love outlasting duty after all.
